idiom: to have a lot on one's plate
meaning: to have many tasks or responsibilities to deal with
example: I can't take on another project this month because I have a lot on my plate.
origin: The origin is uncertain. The image is of food piled high on a plate, which suggests a heavy load of work.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to eat a very large meal at a restaurant
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is a literal reading of the words. The idiom has nothing to do with eating.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to be fired from a job without warning
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes being busy with work, not losing a job.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to finish a task much earlier than expected
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes having a heavy workload, not completing work quickly.

explanation: 'To have a lot on one's plate' means to be very busy with many tasks or responsibilities. It is common in workplace conversations, especially when someone is explaining why they cannot take on new work.
